 News Blink-182 and Bring Me The Horizon will headline Download Festival 2027: dates, full lineup and how to buy tickets
 Here’s how to get tickets for the UK’s biggest rock festival, with Evanescence, Mötley Crüe, Turnstile, Faith No More, Napalm Death and more
 Written by Amy Houghton Contributing writer Friday 13 November 2026 Share Copy Link Facebook Twitter Pinterest Email WhatsApp Photograph: Download | Download 2027 Advertising Next summer’s festival headliners are coming in thick and fast. Fatboy Slim and Robbie Williams are going to be at the Isle of Wight Festival , Phoebe Bridgers has been announced for All Points East  and Bon Jovi is lined up for BST Hyde Park.  Now, the UK’s metalheads have been given something to get excited about. 
 More than 100 acts have just been announced for Download Festival 2027. Pop-punk, goth rock, nu metal, alt rock, death metal – it’s all covered. Headline sets will come from none other than Blink-182, Bring Me The Horizon and Evanescence. 
 Tickets for DLXXIV are on sale this week and are expected to sell out in record time. So, here’s all the info you need if you want to be there.

 When and where is Download Festival 2027?
 The fest is taking place from Wednesday June 9 to Sunday June 13 at  Donington Park in Leicestershire, the ‘spiritual home of rock’.
 Download Festival 2027 headliners
 Blink-182 , Bring Me The Horizon and Evanescence top the bill. 
 Download Festival 2027 lineup so far
 More than 100 artists have been announced, including heavyweights like Turnstile, the Prodigy and a ‘very special performance’ from rock legends Mötley Crüe. Here’s the full Download lineup so far.

 When do tickets go on sale?  
 A PayPal presale is currently live, and general sale will launch at 10am on Sunday November 15. Tickets are available via  Ticketmaster . Only weekend tickets will be up for grabs – day tickets normally go on sale around March or April. 
 Download Festival 2027 ticket prices
 Non-camping weekend (adult): £315 
 Non-camping weekend (child): £174.50
 Five-night general camping (adult): £375
 Five-night general camping (child): £197.50
 Three-night general camping (adult): £355
 Three-night general camping (child): £191.50 
 How to travel to Download Festival
 The closest mainline railway stations to Donington Park are East Midlands Parkway (20 minutes away) and Derby (30 minutes away), which will both be served by regular transfer buses.
 Alternatively, you can book a spot on a Big Green Coach , which will be running services from 81 different UK locations. If you’re planning on taking a car you’ll need to buy a parking pass.
